data.content:
# Overview - MuSig2 (BIP327)

The intro flow promised it: "a multisig that aggregated into one key (MuSig2)." This canvas builds that key - and spends it.

Three signers hold three ordinary keys. MuSig2 aggregates the **public** keys into one; nobody ever holds, or could compute, the matching private key. To spend, each signer contributes a **partial signature** using only their own secret, and the partials sum into one valid 64-byte Schnorr signature. Schnorr's linear structure is what makes the summing work - and why this needed Taproot.

The chain sees `OP_1 <Q>` and a 66-byte key-path witness: byte-for-byte the intro flow's spend. Three signers, zero trace.

The price: two interactive rounds - nonces first, partials second - with everyone online.

The pipeline: SIGNERS → KEYAGG → PREIMAGE → ROUND 1 → ROUND 2 → TRANSACTION.

*Builds on Taproot intro. The signing nodes pass the official BIP327 test vectors.*
data.title: Text Info Node

data.content:
## KeyAgg - three keys become one

Naive addition of public keys is broken: the last signer could craft a key that cancels the others and take sole control. BIP327 prevents this by giving each key a **coefficient** derived from the entire ordered key list, then summing the weighted keys. Every contribution is bound to the full participant set.

Consequence: **order matters**. Same three keys, different order - different aggregate key. Agree on the order before you aggregate.

The aggregate then walks the standard path from the intro: TapTweak → output key Q → P2TR address. From here on, nothing on this canvas knows or cares that Q hides three people.
data.title: Text Info Node

data.content:
## Round 1 - nonces

Each signer generates two secret nonces and publishes only their public halves; the three pubnonces aggregate into one 66-byte session nonce that Round 2 will use.

The randomness feeding each nonce is a visible node so the whole session is reproducible - frozen here as the public test vector of one completed session.

**The one rule of MuSig2:** nonces are fresh every session, used once, destroyed. Reusing a secnonce across different messages lets an attacker solve for your private key with plain algebra. In production, this rule is the protocol.
data.title: Text Info Node

data.content:
## Round 2 - partial signatures

Each signer now computes a partial signature from their own secret key, their own secret nonces, and the shared session values - the aggregate nonce, the message, the key list, the tweak.

A partial is just a 32-byte number. Anyone can add the three together; the aggregation node also folds in the taproot tweak, and the sum is a complete Schnorr signature that verifies against Q like any single-signer spend - though no single signer could have produced it, and the aggregate private key never existed anywhere.
data.title: Text Info Node
